 The `--auto-approve true` flag tells Cline to run autonomously, executing approved tools without waiting for interactive confirmation. Prompt runs start in Act mode by default, so CI/CD workflows can perform the requested work immediately.
 
-### Command Permissions
-We explicitly restrict what commands Cline can run using `CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS`. This ensures Cline can only use `gh` and `git` commands relevant to reviewing, preventing any accidental or malicious system modifications.
+### Command Access
+With `--auto-approve true`, Cline can run any shell command on the runner; the CLI has no allow or deny list for shell commands. The job's `permissions` block is what limits `GH_TOKEN`. To block commands, have the workflow write a `PreToolUse` hook to `~/.cline/hooks/` that cancels `run_commands` calls you don't allow, like the [.clineignore hook](/customization/clineignore#enforcing-clineignore-with-a-hook). Don't rely on a hook in the repository's `.cline/hooks/`: the job checks out the pull request, so the pull request can change it.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in c8bd341b8. Hooks from `.cline/hooks/` and `.clinerules/hooks/` in the checkout join the same list as global hooks and run with `process.env`. Plugins from `.cline/plugins/` also load by default. The section now says the checkout's hooks and plugins run with the job's environment, including `GH_TOKEN`. It gives two ways to stop them: check out the base branch and read the changes with `gh pr diff`, or delete `.cline` and `.clinerules` before the review step. Only after that does it suggest a global `PreToolUse` hook.

</Card>

+## Which products support each control
+
+Cline products read the organization's remote configuration when a member signs in to the organization. The VS Code and JetBrains extensions enforce every control below. Cline Desktop and the CLI apply only some of them, so members who use those products can choose other providers and MCP servers.
+
+| Control | VS Code and JetBrains | CLI | Cline Desktop |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Rules and workflows | Yes | Yes | No |
+| Skills | Yes | No | No |
+| Allowed providers and provider settings | Yes | No | No |
+| Members can't switch organization or use a personal account | Yes | No | No |
+| **Enable MCP Marketplace** (when off, also blocks local MCP servers) | Yes | No | No |
+| **Allow members to use their own servers** (MCP) | Yes | No | No |
+| Organization MCP servers | Yes | No | No |
+| **Cline Telemetry** | Yes | No | No |
+| **Allow YOLO mode** | No | No | No |
+| **Allow Kanban** | No | No | No |
+
+The VS Code and JetBrains extensions show a lock icon on settings that the organization controls. Admins and Owners can choose **Opt out of remote config** on the Account page to work without the organization's settings; members can't.
+
+To choose which products to recommend, check which controls your organization relies on. For example, if members must use only your approved providers, deploy the VS Code or JetBrains extension.
+
+### Files Cline writes to the workspace
+
+To apply the organization's rules and workflows, Cline writes them, and a copy of the organization's settings, into the folder it's working in: `.cline/enterprise/` in the CLI, and `.cline/remote-config/` in the VS Code and JetBrains extensions. Cline rewrites these files when the organization's settings change. Add both folders to your repository's `.gitignore` so that nobody commits them:
+
+```text
+.cline/enterprise/
+.cline/remote-config/
+```

The patterns are now `**/.cline/enterprise/` and `**/.cline/remote-config/`, and the page says why: the cached settings can include prompt storage access keys, and a member may open a subfolder of the repository. `git check-ignore` confirms that the recursive patterns match a nested folder and the root-anchored ones don't.
